items.title: Updates to Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access in macOS
items.summary: For decades, Mac computers have been loved by creators and developers who build, automate, and innovate using cutting-edge technologies and tools. We want to keep empowering our community in these pursuits, while helping our users stay safe and in control of their data and privacy. In macOS 27.3 beta 2 today, we’re introducing increased transparency and more granular options for two of the APIs: Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access. Before granting an app such extraordinary access, users should understand that it puts all of the data on their Mac at risk. These changes are designed to help them do that and to empower them to make informed decisions about their own data and privacy. The changes include:A split of Device Control and Data Access into two settings: (1) System & App Protection Override, and (2) Accessibility A single method for granting permissions by selecting the requesting app from a listGuidance to encourage users to grant access to just the specific apps (for System & App Protection Override) or folders (for Full Disk Access) that are required for their workflowsIncreased visibility into the wide range of data apps will receive access to or control over if full permissions are grantedThe option for users to configure apps to ask every time they require accessA transparency indicator when a requesting app is controlling another app using System & App Protection OverrideDevelopers should be prepared to adjust how they onboard users and make sure their apps can gracefully handle having access to only a limited set of folders or apps when utilizing these APIs. Users will see these updates when approving new app permission requests. All app permissions previously granted by users will remain in effect.Developers of apps that use Full Disk Access for disk backup, or the new Accessibility settings to provide assistive technologies, can request entitlements to deliver the same experience for new installations that they offered before macOS 27.3. Currently, known apps aren’t affected and will keep the same experience without an entitlement. Additional entitlement details will be available soon.
